newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares end firmer after rate cut,off highs.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares end firmer after rate cut,off highs.

text.p: Italian shares ended firmer in heavy volume on Wednesday as the market welcomed a long-awaited cut in the Bank of Italy's key interest rates but gains were pared by the close of the session on Wall Street's early fall, traders said.

Very large buying orders were seen in the afternoon flowing in from domestic brokers on behalf of investment funds. The Dow's initial fall on a selloff of IBM shares just took the edge of gains. "Our market looks like it's in for quite a bullish period," one trader said, noting the switch in Italian investor interest from debt to equities.
The All-share Mibtel index ended up 1.7 percent at 12,431 and the Mib30 blue chip index ended 1.53 percent higher at 18,603.
The Mibtel posted a session high at 12,524 after an opening 12,490 while the Mib30 touched 18,783 after an 18,745 start.
"Funds just dare not stay underweight," one trader said, while selective foreign buying was also seen, particularly late in the session on insurer Generali and carmaker Fiat.

Generali ended 2.71 percent up at 32,100 lire and Fiat closed 2.25 percent higher at 5,170. Olivetti, the most heavily traded stock, finished 4.87 percent up at 714.3 lire with over 107 million shares exchanging hands.
Banks were all firmer, with Credito Italiano up 5.76 percent up at 2,150 following an "outperform" from Goldman Sachs.

Telecoms performed poorly, with Telecom Italia off 0.71 percent to 4,729 lire and mobile phone operator TIM down 0.39 percent to 4,848. Traders said current uncertainty in the Italian telecoms sector was weighing on the stocks which are traditionally seen as attractive.
One dealer added that a large sell order for Telecom Italia is in course while TIM was seeing profit-taking after recent rises.
